contexts.text: That that nation had no Conjugial... is evident from (the permission of polygamy) among them; for where there is the Conjugial understood in the spiritual sense... this is by no means permitted. Explained. AC 9002:end. AC 10603:5.
Love truly conjugial is never possible (in polygamy). HH 379, Explained. SE 4409. DeConj 120.

The reason a more internal religion was not opened by Mohammed, was on account of polygamy, which exhales uncleanness towards Heaven; for the marriage of a husband with one wife corresponds to the marriage of the Lord and the Church.

Polygamy was permitted them because they are Orientals, who without this permission would have burned for foul adulteries more than Europeans, and would have perished. CL 342:end. TCR 833:end. SE 5061. DeConj 46.
A religion which ordains that it is not allowable to marry a number of wives... is rejected by those who for ages have been polygamists.

(There was no polygamy in the Golden Age); for they could not think of more than one wife. With those who did so, the heavenly blessednesses of their souls instantly withdrew... to the extremes of their bodies... and together therewith the distinguished marks of virility; and when this was perceived they were cast out of the land.
(The people of the Copper Age) replied, Are not polygamical marriages scortatory?
If polygamists invade us, they are cast out into the darkness of the north; (which) is dullness of the mind and ignorance of Truths.
(The people of the Iron Age) live with two or three wives, and some with more; because they are delighted with variety, obedience, and honour as of Majesty. Explained.
There flowed out from the women's apartment a libidinous effluvium, (which) was from polygamical love, which is connubial, and at the same time scortatory.

That chastity is predicable of monogamical marriages only... For conjugial love enters according to the increase of wisdom, and this according to the implantation of the Church by the Lord. This cannot be effected with polygamists, because they divide conjugial love; and this love, when divided, is not unlike the love of the sex, which, in itself, is natural.

You will rarely meet a man who will not reply in favour of polygamical marriage; and this is the love of the sex: but... almost all women will reject polygamical marriages; from which it follows that with women there is the love of one of the sex; thus conjugial love.
Concerning polygamy. Chapter.
(Polygamy, with a Christian, is both natural and spiritual adultery.) Explained.

By polygamical marriage in the Christian world, the marriage of the Lord and the Church is profaned; likewise the marriage of good and truth; and, above all, the Word; and, with the Word, the Church. Signified, Explained.
(Thus) the damnation of Christian polygamists after death is more grievous than that of those who commit only natural adultery. Described.
Why polygamical marriages were permitted to the Israelitish nation. Explained.
To such, polygamy is not hurtful; for it is inscribed on the natural man...
That polygamy is not in harmony with the Divine law. Illustrated.
(Why polygamy is permitted to the Mohammedans.) Explained.
In the lower Mohammedan Heaven they (practise polygamy).
The quality of the heat of the conjugial love of polygamists... was perceived by me like the foul heat of a bath.
That polygamy is lasciviousness. Explained.

Polygamical love is love divided among a number, and divided love is not conjugial love... Hence the former love is lascivious, and polygamy is lasciviousness. The reason polygamical love is the love of the sex, is that it differs only in being limited to the number which the polygamist may take...

The reason polygamical love is a love of the external or natural man, is that it is inscribed on this man; and whatever the natural man does from himself is evil... and evil in regard to the sex... is scortation; but, as this is ruinous to society, in place of scortation there has been induced its likeness, which is called polygamy.
That conjugial chastity, purity, and holiness are not possible with polygamists. Explained.
That a polygamist, so long as he remains a polygamist, cannot become spiritual. Explained.
That polygamy is not sin with those with whom it exists from religion. Explained.
To prevent polygamy from being sin to them, they remain natural...
And hence do not know that there is anything of evil, or of lasciviousness, in polygamy.
That polygamy is not sin with those who are in ignorance about the Lord. Explained.
Hence comes polygamy.
(Such a man) is not to blame if... he believes polygamical love to be the only conjugial love.
That of these, although polygamists, those are saved who acknowledge God, and from religion live according to the civil laws of justice. Explained.
But that no (polygamists whatever) can be consociated with the Angels in the Christian Heavens. Explained.
That there is (only) natural jealousy with polygamists. Explained.
Conjugial love with polygamists is natural.
The jealous fire into which polygamical conjugial love breaks out is anger and revenge. Explained.
With more than one (mistress) there is what is polygamical within, which induces on men a state merely natural...
That (concubinage conjointly with a wife) is polygamy, which... is to be damned out of the Christian world. Explained.
This Christian Conjugial perishes through polygamical scortation; (or rather) with a Christian polygamist it is closed up and intercepted; but is resuscitable in his descendants.
That this Conjugial is destroyed, with a Christian, by polygamical scortation, is very evident from the fact, that he cannot, like a Mohammedan polygamist, love a concubine and a wife equally...
(Such charity and faith) are from a polygamical bed or marriage. Explained.
The vastation of those in Christendom who had confirmed themselves in polygamy. Described. DeConj 44.

If a Christian man were to marry a number of wives, it would be as if he had two Churches with him; and also as if truth were to derive its essence from two goods... Hence it is that love truly conjugial is never possible between one man and a number of wives; for thus it would be lasciviousness which would enter; and besides love cannot be divided, because it is from the affection of the one according with the thought of the other; and this unanimity, and cohabitation, which makes the essence of conjugial love, is not possible (with a number). In a word, with such there is not the Christian Church; and therefore when an Angel in Heaven merely thinks about a plurality of wives, the Celestial and the Angelic perish; both the joy and the wisdom with him; and he falls from Heaven. DeConj 45.

In the other life, the Mohammedans at first take a number of wives, besides concubines; but as, in the Spiritual World, there is a conjunction of lower minds, and those of a different lower mind cannot be together, they separate of their own accord, and at last are conjoined with such a woman as is of a like lower mind. Thus do they gradually separate themselves from their women, and are at last united to one... But those who persist in polygamy, in course of time become so invalidated and impotent that they nauseate marriage, because it carries what is lascivious with it.
Those of them who are in their Heaven have only one wife; they have rejected a plurality...
